A1.justification: Both PDFs describe seq-JEPA. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite extensive reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original representation-learning experiments, ablations, path-integration results and ImageNet-1k transfer evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds OOD rotation, predictor-retrieval, computational-cost and high-compute evaluations.

M1.justification: The encoder, learned action embeddings, transformer aggregator, action-conditioned MLP predictor, EMA target encoder and cosine prediction loss remain unchanged. Saliency sampling and inhibition of return also remain. Additional explanations and baseline variants do not establish changes to seq-JEPA itself.

E1.justification: v3 adds a focused coverage extension: 3DIEBench evaluation on rotations outside the training range, using (-π,-π/2) and (π/2,π). The original datasets, transformation tasks, saccade/path-integration settings and ImageNet-1k transfer evaluation remain.

E2.justification: VICRegTraj, VICReg with viewpoint trajectory regularization, is newly evaluated on 3DIEBench, CIFAR100 and Tiny ImageNet. Existing baseline methods remain. Transformer-projector baseline variants were already described in v1; v3 supplies their separate numerical results.

E3.justification: v3 adds predictor evaluation using MRR, Hit@1 and Hit@5, a disjoint-angle OOD testing protocol, and a high-compute experiment using 2000 epochs, 256×256 images and batch size 1024. These supplement the retained standard 3DIEBench setting of 1000 epochs, 128×128 images and batch size 512.

E4.justification: v3 adds OOD robustness, high-compute sensitivity and systematic runtime/FLOP analyses, and publishes results for transformer-projector controls already described in v1. Conversely, Table 4 loses the random-noise and nonlearnable-action-embedding ablations, and v1 Appendix B.2's direct test of aggregate-representation invariance is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random seeds for path integration and action-conditioning ablations, retaining the same uncertainty conventions. The added evaluations introduce no new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v3 adds baseline, cost, OOD, retrieval and high-compute results; notably, seq-JEPA (3,3) obtains relative-rotation R² = -0.71 on the new OOD test. Most original main-table scores remain unchanged. However, the appendix classification score for 3DIEBench (3,3) changes from 86.14% to 85.32%, while v3 Table 1 still reports 86.14%. Several STL-10 appendix entries also change, and Table 3 newly reports SimCLR positional R² = -0.06.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of invariance and equivariance, aggregation equation and prediction objective remain equivalent. Separating the predictor expression into a numbered equation adds no new mathematical result. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: v1's abstract and introduction explicitly describe the aggregate representation as invariant; v3 softens this to effectiveness for invariance-demanding tasks. The central contributions—architecturally separated representations, competitive downstream performance and sequential observation integration—remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of OOD failure as a transformation-geometry shift and hypothesizes that aggregation preserves semantic information despite failed equivariance. It expands explanations of sequence-length benefits, introduces convergence and compute-sensitivity interpretations, and explicitly acknowledges the limitation to short contexts. These go beyond v1's explanations based mainly on complementary observations.

D1.justification: v3 adds documented links to code, models, saliency maps and the OOD dataset. It also supplies detailed runtime/FLOP information, OOD rendering hardware and time, high-compute hardware, the VICRegTraj loss coefficient, and ImageNet saliency-processing details including the MIT1003 center-bias prior. Existing optimizer and architecture specifications are largely retained or relocated.

R1.justification: v3 extends discussion to trajectory regularization, Chavhan et al.'s feature-head ensembles and context-scaling/frozen-backbone research, while dropping the masked-image-modeling discussion and associated citations. Its central positioning within JEPA and equivariant SSL remains, with a more detailed distinction from ContextSSL.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and substantial portions of the methods, results and limitations are rewritten. Related work moves after the results, saccade learning and path integration are merged, and path-integration details move to the appendix. These constitute extensive narrative restructuring beyond added experiments.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two-column to single-column layout. The architecture diagram is redrawn, the opening performance plot moves into the results, and the conditioned STL-10 UMAP moves to the appendix. Six additional tables and extensive resizing and rearrangement substantially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 improves assessability through explicit projector-control results, retrieval evaluation, OOD failure reporting, compute comparisons and resource links. These strengthen validation and reproducibility. However, removing the direct invariance test and two ablations reduces supporting evidence, while the new 86.14% versus 85.32% inconsistency between Tables 1 and 12 weakens numerical reliability. The net improvement is useful but qualified.
